sentences.text: Mercury orbits so close to the Sun that we can only see it in twilight, low near the horizon.
This morning it stands nineteen and a half degrees west of the Sun, at its greatest angular distance: it appears on the eastern horizon before sunrise.
Elongation is the moment we look at the inner planet's orbit tangentially from Earth.
Seen from above the geometry is clear: the Sun–Mercury line falls perpendicular to the line of sight from Earth.
Mercury repeats this cycle roughly every one hundred sixteen days; the next evening elongation comes in January.
